channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: Minsk-Karachi railway shows Eurasia’s quiet geopolitical rewiring
item.description: The news that Pakistan, Russia, and Belarus are working on a test freight railway connecting Minsk, Moscow, and Karachi may seem like just another infrastructure project needing funding and construction. However, the real importance of this initiative lies in what it shows about the rapid shift in Eurasia’s economic geography.

item.title: Olivia Rodrigo's festival is uniting women and girls behind nonprofits promoting their well-being
item.description: Daisy Chain Fields on Saturday (Aug 29) united a women-led lineup boasting queer pop star Chappell Roan, breakout rapper Doechii and riot grrrl pioneers Bikini Kill behind issues of women's health, workplace protections and legal rights. Olivia Rodrigo's festival is uniting women and girls behind nonprofits promoting their well-being.

item.title: US Conducts Fresh Strikes On Iranian Launchers, Seen As "Signal' To Tehran On Hormuz
item.description: US forces struck two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz after the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) was observed preparing to launch rockets carrying sea mines into the vital waterway, a US official confirmed to RFE/RL. US Strike On Iranian Launchers Signals Resolve To Keep Hormuz Open, Experts Say. US Conducts Fresh Strikes On Iranian Launchers, Seen As "Signal' To Tehran On Hormuz.

item.title: What a cancer survivor’s wrongful dismissal case tells us about the employer-employee relationship
item.description: When illness strikes or life gets in the way, employees will become temporarily less available to their employers. This is normal and should not be an exception to be managed away, say SUSS professor Victor Seah and Singapore Cancer Society’s Tan Kwang Cheak. What a cancer survivor’s wrongful dismissal case tells us about the employer-employee relationship.

item.title: Ukrainian Officials Blamed For 'Negligence' After Deadly Strikes
item.description: With at least 38 people killed in Russian air attacks on the Kyiv region, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said "terrible negligence" was a factor in the high death toll. Ukrainian authorities have pledged to investigate why a weapons storage depot was located close to a populated area. Ukrainian Officials Blamed for 'Negligence' After Deadly Strikes.

item.title: Nepal struggles to preserve recovered bodies as flood toll touches 788
item.description: More than 900 workers are missing from hydropower sites and officials believe around 100 people trapped inside tunnels are alive; experts from India, China, and South Korea have joined the Nepal Army’s efforts to rescue these workers Nepal struggles to preserve recovered bodies as flood toll touches 788.

item.title: ‘The lake is our life’: Protecting a shared lifeline in Uganda
item.description: On the shores of Nkondo, in Uganda’s Kikuube district, the day begins before sunrise. Fishers enter the lake to fish, while families around Lake Albert rely on its waters for food, income and daily survival. ‘The lake is our life’: Protecting a shared lifeline in Uganda.

item.description: Bangladesh’s planned J-10CE purchase could significantly strengthen its airpower while tying that capability more closely to Chinese weapons, support networks and supply chains. item.title: Zelenskyy Blasts 'Negligence' As Ukraine Mourns Dozens Killed In Russian Strike
item.description: Ukrainian rescue crews early on August 30 continued to search for victims of the deadly Russian attack outside of Kyiv, while local residents -- as well as President Volodymyr Zelenskyy -- demanded answers as to why explosives were stored in a warehouse so near private housing. Zelenskyy Blasts 'Negligence' As Ukraine Mourns Dozens Killed In Russian Strike.

item.title: Was it a mistake for 99 Colombian guerrillas to lay down their arms?
item.description: ‘Total peace’ plan of previous government led only 99 of Colombia’s 30,000 armed combatants to disarm, but new president Abelardo De la Espriella opposes peace agreementsIn mid-June, 99 guerrilla fighters were flown by helicopter to a small settlement in a rural area of southern Colombia where they lined up and, one by one, handed their weapons to government officials: rifles, pistols, machine gun.

item.description: US President Donald Trump’s abrupt directive on August 16, 2026, to drastically scale back the joint “Ulchi Freedom Shield” (UFS) military exercises sent shockwaves across the Asia-Pacific geostrategic landscape. item.title: Bangladesh should join the Mecca pact – if the bargain’s real
item.description: Bangladesh’s problem is not its geography. It is a geopolitical imagination too often confined by geography. So long as Dhaka views its foreign policy almost exclusively through the South Asian frame, India will remain the dominant power around which every Bangladeshi calculation revolves. item.title: Russia's 'Make Or Break' Airliner Approaches Production Amid Sanctions And Shortages
item.description: An "all-Russian" MC-21 passenger jet made its first test flight in early August, marking a step closer to full production, due to begin in 2027. But years of geopolitical turbulence have pushed the project far off-course, aviation insiders say. Russia's 'Make Or Break' Airliner Approaches Production Amid Sanctions And Shortages.
